correctness.rationale: The finite strongly separated similarity systems have the stated Moran roots. For the countable system, finite subsystems give the lower bound and all level-k cylinders give a cover with vanishing power sum at every exponent above the zeta-pressure root. The symbolic Bernoulli weights at either root give both shift invariance and conformality; the accumulation point 1 is not an extra symbol. At d=(1+sz)/q, a decreasing-function sum-integral comparison has error at most s after multiplication by s, uniformly for bounded real z. This and s^(sz)→1 bracket the finite root on either side of its unique limit even for τ<1; the zeta pole brackets the full root in positive z. At a fixed u>0 the same comparison on the partial sum gives the continuous limiting CDF, with the atom at u=0 vanishing. Finally, the strict threshold test is exactly sH_N>1; at first crossing, 0<H_N−1/s≤1/N for small s, yielding log N=1/s−γ+o(1). No computation is needed for these proofs; the supplied program was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: No formal certificate or new numerical replay. Limits are at fixed q and fixed τ and are for symbolic digits, not ambient measures.

Evaluate it at b=(qd−1)/ε→λz (z=z_τ or 1), and cutoff σ=uε/s for any fixed 0<u<τ in the finite case or any u>0 for the full case. The root-weight multiplier s^(qd)/ε→λ, so the resulting limit is exactly ∫_0^u exp(−zv)dv. This is the CDF itself; endpoints follow from support/continuity. originality.rationale: The earlier October 11 result changes both q and c, but after writing x=qd and s=c^(1/q) the pressure and all digit weights are exactly (s/n)^x, with no q dependence. Thus the different parameter paths in physical coordinates do not produce different pressure or digit problems. The October theorem gives both dimension asymptotics through this substitution, and its uniform harmonic-sum formula directly gives each limiting conformal CDF at the already-determined exponent. The remaining Euler cutoff uses the universal pressure at x=1 and the classical constant term in H_N; the November 8 comparison explicitly gives the same formula in its parameter a=s. This is coverage by implication, not a claim that October literally states the digit theorem or that later work has historical priority.
